yinnon (H5125, from nin 'offspring'): Rashi, Metzudat Zion and one view in Meiri take it as 'rule, lordship' (cf. Prov 29:21 manon); Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri and Malbim take it from nin 'offspring', a niphal 'be propagated, sprout'. I follow the offspring sense, which the Hebrew 'son/grandson' pair nin and neked supports (Gen 21:23 uses them together), and render 'be continued/sprout' with the 'rule' reading in the commentary. The cross-reference to Ps 74:8 'ninam' is Rashi's, which I could not verify as the same root.

The five English versions split on verb 8: KJV/ASV/Webster 'be blessed in him' (passive, niphal sense), YLT/BBE 'bless themselves' (reflexive). The Hebrew is hitpael, so I choose the reflexive. Likewise the final verb is a piel of 'ashar, 'call happy/fortunate', not a plain 'bless'; KJV 'call him blessed' blurs it with barak.
